sources.title: Leslie Pack Kaelbling, Michael L. Littman, and Anthony R. Cassandra, Planning and Acting in Partially Observable Stochastic Domains, Brown University Technical Report CS-96-08
sources.locator: Complete 29-page PDF inspected. §§3.1–3.4, PDF pp. 8–11: finite POMDP model, belief definition, Bayes update, and belief-MDP reduction. §§4.1–4.3, PDF pp. 11–16: policy trees, state-conditional alpha vectors, finite-horizon value envelope, backup, and pruning. The source permits action-dependent observations O(s′,a,o); this batch uses the plan's action-independent specialization O(o|s′).

contents.name: Finite POMDP model and the next-state observation convention; the local model specializes the paper's action-dependent observation law
Finite Bayes belief update on positive-likelihood observations, with the zero-normalizer boundary excluded from the quotient
Belief-state sufficient statistic and belief-MDP transition/reward interpretation; the full local factorization proof is supplied here
Policy-tree recursion and state-conditional alpha-vector values; the exhaustive finite backup is authored locally
Finite-horizon value as the maximum of finitely many linear policy-tree values and safe removal of vectors with no maximizing belief; the complete proof is supplied locally
The paper's optimized linear-program witness-search implementation and its polynomial-time accounting
contents.reason: The authored algorithm exhaustively enumerates finite policy trees and makes no LP implementation, witness-search termination, or polynomial-time claim.

sources.title: Russ Tedrake, Planning Under Uncertainty: Partially-observable Markov decision processes, MIT Underactuated Robotics course notes
sources.locator: Complete relevant course-note page inspected, lines 13–24: finite discrete POMDP model, belief as a conditional distribution, sufficient-statistic statement, Bayes update, observation marginal, and belief-MDP transition. The local proofs do not rely on the note's diagram or use of a finite reachable-belief set as the full belief simplex.

Action-independent observation likelihood and finite Bayes update

The fixed-horizon reachable beliefs are finite because the finite action-observation history set is finite; no finiteness of the whole simplex is claimed
Piecewise-linear-convex theorem and proof of alpha-vector recursion
contents.reason: This page does not provide that proof; the full local finite policy-tree induction is supplied in the theorem.

sources.title: Pascal Poupart, CS 886 Lecture 13: POMDPs, University of Waterloo
sources.locator: Complete 19-page lecture PDF inspected. Slides 3–8: finite POMDP model, history, belief update, conditional-plan trees, and linear plan values. Slides 9–15: finite-horizon piecewise-linear-convex claim, dynamic-programming backup, and pruning. Slide 19 gives the representation-size recurrence |Γₖ₊₁|=|A||Γₖ|^{|O|}; the local proof distinguishes policy-tree counts from duplicate alpha vectors.

contents.name: Finite POMDP state/action/observation model, finite horizon, and belief update
Policy-tree conditional plans and linear value at an initial belief
Finite-horizon piecewise-linear-convex value and dynamic-programming/pruning context; full proof is local
Slide 19 representation-size recurrence; the explicit family with exponentially many distinct witnessed vectors is constructed and proved locally

sources.title: Bob Dumas and John E. McCarthy, Transition to Higher Mathematics, §1.2: Sets
sources.locator: Complete relevant page inspected, lines 205–242 and 244–262. Lines 226–232 identify the set of natural numbers less than n as a canonical set with exactly n elements; lines 244–262 explain set extensionality. The local proof derives I_n=n from the library’s additive-order/membership theorem and derives |I_n|=n from its finite-cardinality definition.

contents.name: A natural number n canonically determines the initial segment of natural numbers less than n, with exactly n elements

canonical.name: Finite initial-segment cardinality needed for the explicit clocked witness family
canonical.argument: Proved locally from the published additive-order/membership theorem and finite-cardinality definition; no external source result is claimed.
